# Surface and Mesh Extraction
## Overview
This family provides methods to extract explicit 3D geometry (meshes or segmented primitives) from trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models, which are inherently implicit volumetric representations. Unlike [3D Gaussian Splatting](1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) which renders images directly, these methods convert the Gaussian parameters into structured geometric outputs. [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) extracts meshes via density field isosurfacing, [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) aligns splats to pre-existing meshes, and [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) segments primitives using 2D-to-3D label propagation.
## Shared principles
All methods operate on a trained set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G} = \{g_i\}_{i=1}^N$, where each $g_i$ is defined by center $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $o_i$, and spherical harmonics coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$. The core challenge is that 3DGS lacks explicit surface topology. Methods either accumulate opacity/density into a voxel grid, calculate distances to external geometric priors, or project 2D segmentation masks into 3D space via multi-view voting. All rely on the standard 3DGS rendering pipeline for depth or color estimation if explicit geometry is not directly available from the primitives.
## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
Extracts a triangulated mesh by building a volumetric density field from Gaussian opacities and applying marching cubes. It differs from [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) by relying on opacity-based density accumulation rather than signed distance functions, and from [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) by operating directly on the 3D primitive structure rather than lifting 2D features. Choose when a training-free, explicit mesh is required from a standard 3DGS model.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
Connects a large-scale triangular mesh with 3D Gaussian splats by classifying primitives as tightly-bound or loosely-bound based on their distance to the mesh surface, while masking out splats occluded by the mesh. It differs from sibling methods like [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) by explicitly leveraging a pre-existing geometric mesh to prune redundant volume and align appearance, rather than relying solely on opacity field thresholding or segmentation. Choose when refining a known mesh or reducing Gaussian count via geometric priors.

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
Segments 3D Gaussian primitives in a volume visualization scene by lifting 2D segmentation masks from a reference view into 3D space using multi-view label voting. It solves the problem of partial scene editing by decomposing a basic scene into distinct parts, allowing independent color, opacity, and lighting adjustments. Unlike sibling methods that require learnable feature vectors or density fields, this approach is training-free and relies on external segmentation models and geometric projection. Choose when interactive scene editing or part-level decomposition is needed.

### Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction
Extracts a textured mesh by converting rendered depth and normal maps into an oriented colored point cloud, which is then input into a Poisson reconstruction algorithm.
- [S1, unofficial] Render depth maps from training views using median depth values from splats projected onto pixels.
- [S1, unofficial] Convert the rendered depth maps back into 3D space to derive corresponding normal maps.
- [S1, unofficial] Generate an oriented colored point cloud from the RGB image, depth map, and normal map.
- [S1, unofficial] Input the oriented colored point cloud into the Poisson extraction method to create the textured mesh.

## Background
Originating from the need to obtain explicit geometry from implicit radiance fields, these methods extend 3DGS beyond novel view synthesis. [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) and [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) address the lack of surface definition in standard splatting. [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) adapts 2D segmentation tools for 3D Gaussian manipulation. The Poisson variant leverages traditional computer vision pipelines adapted for Gaussian projections.
